terra.problem: The text does not say the person is looking back on the years.
The passage does not say feeling stronger belongs to youth.
It assigns the Teacher an intention to make the reader feel the gray picture, which the text does not state.
The text does not say the house has gone through a lot.
The text says those grinding are few, not that their number dwindled.
The text does not say the quietness of the house is why the bird's sound gets the person up.
The hired rooster invents a new part of Papa Dorin's world.
The text says a person rises at the bird's sound; it does not say the sound wakes the person.
The text does not say the house is so hushed that a bird is enough to get someone up.
The text says men fear heights and dangers of the road, not that they are growing afraid.
Saying he will not joke comments on how he tells the passage.
The text calls it man's eternal home but does not say whether it is a place on a map.
The punchline jokes about how Scripture is written by counting broken things in a sentence.
It says only one object is golden, though the text does not state what the pitcher and wheel are made of.
The text does not say none of the objects is brand new. Being broken does not establish their age.
The reference to rushing to the next card exposes the lesson's structure to the baker.
